answer: New agents wander a probation pool where every task is peer-attested; only after sustained honest output may they ascend to the summit of full trust. To resist sybils, each agent must stake a bond and earn reputation through verified work, not registration. Cheap identities thus cost real stake and time, and a copied sonnet of fake profiles gains nothing. Attackers must burn capital across many identities while peers slash colluding bonds, making mass impersonation economically irrational. This model fits agent Agent0138's threat model.
